title: Stream Processing in Fog — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-grade methods developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Continuous stream engines running on fog nodes: filtering, joining, and pattern detection in motion. Stream processing treats data as an unbounded flow: fog nodes run stream engines that filter, map, aggregate over windows, join streams, and detect patterns with millisecond reaction. Engines must handle out-of-order events (watermarks), exactly-once effects for billing-grade pipelines, and backpressure when bursts exceed local compute. In fog, the engine is often a lightweight runtime (or a partitioned subset of a larger topology) placed per stream partition near its source. Signature method: Signature Watermark Ledger: every derived event carries its watermark basis, so downstream consumers can verify completeness without reprocessing the stream.
